title: Tapering strategies in elite British endurance runners
authors: Spilsbury KL, Fudge BW, Ingham SA, Faulkner SH, Nimmo MA
population: Elite British middle-distance (800/1500 m), long-distance (3000 m steeplechase to 10,000 m) and marathon runners
findings: Taper duration median (IQR): 6 (3) days in middle distance, 6 (1) in long distance and 14 (8) days in marathon runners.
Continuous running volume was reduced to 70 (16)%, 71 (24)% and 53 (12)% of regular levels in MD, LD and MAR runners; interval volume to 53 (45)%, 67 (23)% and 64 (34)%.
Peak interval intensity during taper was above race speed in LD and MAR runners (112 (27)% and 114 (3)%), not different from race speed in MD (100 (2)%).

Higher weekly continuous volume and frequency in regular training were associated with greater reductions during taper (R = -0.70 and R = -0.63); regular-training intensity predicted taper intensity (R = 0.97 continuous, 0.81 interval); algorithms to predict taper content were generated.
limitations: Survey of elite athletes describing practice, not outcomes; no performance comparison across strategies; sample size not stated in abstract; elite practice may not transfer to recreational runners.
implications: Real-world marathon benchmark: taper about 14 days, continuous volume about 53% of regular, interval volume about 64%, interval pace around 114% of race speed.
Distance scaling default band: 5-10 km about 6 days, marathon about 14 days.
Heavier pre-taper weeks get larger absolute and proportional cuts.

verification.notes: Crossref issued 5 Sep 2014 (online); Europe PMC year 2015 (print issue); 2015 kept. Researcher claim 'interval pace around 114% of race speed (faster than race pace, short reps)' - 'short reps' is not in the abstract and was removed.
